newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Airlines and shippers condemn new Dutch cargo fee.
newsitem.headline: Airlines and shippers condemn new Dutch cargo fee.

text.p: Airlines and shippers have reacted angrily to a new fee being proposed by Dutch handlers.
Dutch handling companies are testing market reaction to a new 35 guilder ($18.03) fee which is proposed for introduction on July 1, said a spokesman for the Netherlands handling association, NVLA.

Handlers claim that they are having to do more administration work because a significant amount of cargo is heavier when it arrives at the handling company, than the booked weight on the airwaybill. If a consignment is heavier the 35 guilder fee is then charged directly to the airlines.
One airline source said that sometimes the fee is above the 35 guilders per consignment and can rise to 50 guilders.

The Schiphol airfreight community is only just ridding itself of a 15 guilder acceptance fee which is a flat fee charged to forwarders by the handlers for accepting cargo. This fee will be abandoned on July 1 after several years of wrangling over the charge.

"The airlines will not accept the 35 guilder fee. However, we do accept that there is more pressure on the handling companies from the airlines to check the cargo, weigh it and check its dimensions," said Fred Veenendaal, chairman of Dagsa, the Dutch general sales agents association, representing 74 airlines.

But if the forwarding agents did their job properly there would be no need for such a charge. But there may be a danger of carriers trying to avoid such charges and picking goods up directly from the shippers, he added.
Achim van der Graaff, chairman of the Dutch air cargo carriers association, ACAN, said airlines reject the fee and will refuse to pay it.
Hans Leijgraaff, spokesman for EVO the Dutch shippers organisation, said the fee will eventually be passed on to shippers.
He said it was particularly galling in light of the fact the 15 guilder acceptance charge is just about to be abandoned after many years.
"Handlers should not invent another new fee. Shippers are sick of it," he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
